caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular section filled with a repeated geometric pattern composed of interconnected hexagonal and rectangular shapes, resembling a honeycomb structure. The design is rendered in thin, precise black ink lines on an off-white or yellowed paper background. Each hexagonal shape is formed by short, straight lines arranged with regular spacing, while the rectangles are filled with similar linear cross-hatching. The rectangular patterned area is centered horizontally on the page with ample blank space surrounding it on all sides. To the right of the patterned section, there is handwritten text in black ink, which reads: “Honeycomb Linen. Linen, woven on our own loom in Frederick County, Maryland 1850. M.A.R.S.” The letters "M.A.R.S." and a small asterisk also appear at the lower right corner of the patterned area. There are a few small, irregular brownish stains or marks scattered mostly on the blank areas of the paper. The overall composition places emphasis on the central patterned section and the handwritten note to the right.
title: Coverlet
